brief.headline: Push for Sayaji's ₹66.48/KG price — you're already paying it to them, and this supplier is 13.6% higher for the same dextrose.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹66.48/KG, the price Sayaji Industries gives you for the same dextrose.
priceAsk.basis: You pay them ₹75.51/KG today, but Sayaji already delivers identical dextrose at ₹66.48/KG — a 13.6% gap. The market asking price for Anhydrous Dextrose IP sits in a ₹60–81/kg band (typically ₹66–73/kg), so ₹66.48 is well inside market-fair range. Hold them to the best price you already pay.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 Days After Receipt — no reason to move.

brief.financialLeverage: They're a ₹514.62 Cr company keeping about ₹4 of every ₹100 they sell (3.7%), so they're not drowning but also not flush with cash. They're growing fast — 21.4% per year — which means they want new orders to fill that capacity. You're tiny to them: your ₹59.65 L is just 0.12% of their sales, so on your own you have almost no pull. The play is to bundle volume or dangle a multi-year commitment in exchange for matching Sayaji's price, and quietly line up Gulshan or Sanstar so you can walk if they won't move.

evidence.point: You pay them ₹75.51/KG but already get ₹66.48/KG from Sayaji for the same dextrose
Market asking price for Anhydrous Dextrose IP typically sits at ₹66–73/kg
They're growing sales fast and want volume
You're a tiny customer to them
evidence.figure: ₹59.65 L spend = 0.12% of their ₹514.62 Cr revenue

evidence.point: They keep a thin slice of every sale

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker (₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health B 62/100) — an established dextrose supplier and a drop-in alternate; stronger than Universal on both size and financial health.

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (₹821.13 Cr revenue, health C 53/100) focused on starch and dextrose with growing capacity — a credible second source to keep pressure on.

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore maize wet-miller (₹365.39 Cr revenue) making Dextrose ANHYDROUS in IV-fluid grade — exact form match; confirm IP monograph certificate of analysis before switching.

risks: You're 0.12% of their sales — too small to matter unless you bundle more volume or commit longer term.
They're growing fast (21.4%/yr), so they may push back saying capacity is tight and premium pricing reflects demand.
If you squeeze too hard without a qualified backup in your pocket, you risk them walking and leaving you short — line up Gulshan or Sanstar with an RFQ before the meeting.
Their financial health is middling (C 58/100) and margin is thin (3.7%) — a deep cut might spook them or force a quality corner; frame the ask as 'match the market' not 'take a loss'.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to continue with you, but we need to talk about price — we're paying you ₹75.51 a kilo when Sayaji gives us ₹66.48 for identical dextrose, and we'd like to understand how we close that gap.
